I have been farming this land since I was a teenager. I know Quzhou's soil and seasons the way I know my own hands. My 3 mu is the same land rotated between wheat and maize — wheat goes in after maize harvest in October, maize goes in after wheat harvest in June. Same 3 mu, two crops a year. I have done this for decades and I will do it the same way again.

My son works in the city now. There are only two of us at home. I do most of the farm work myself, so I cannot afford too many complications. I rely on what I know works here: standard fertilizer from the village cooperative, the seed varieties my neighbors and I have used for years, and the well when rain is short.

For wheat, I use an improved variety — the kind the cooperative recommends, not the old seeds my mother used, but nothing too expensive either. I apply fertilizer in two rounds: a base application before sowing, and urea at jointing in the spring. I irrigate three times — at sowing, at jointing, and before grain filling. That is what the land here needs. I spray herbicide in early spring and a fungicide before heading. After maize harvest, I do rotary tillage to chop the straw into the soil.

For summer maize, I always use hybrid seed — that I learned maybe twenty years ago and never went back. I plant right after wheat harvest in June. Summer has more rain so I only irrigate twice, once at planting and once if there is a dry spell around tasseling. I apply fertilizer as a base and again at the big bell stage. I spray herbicide after emergence and watch for corn borer. I do rotary tillage before planting.

I will not change this plan. It gave me stable yields last year. At my age, stable is good.
